events.title: Microsoft previews remote lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
events.summary: Microsoft has released a preview of a feature that lets IT administrators remotely lock lost, stolen or compromised Windows devices via Intune, signing out sessions and enforcing a persistent lock screen without wiping the device. It applies to Windows 10 and 11 and several Windows Server versions.
events.why_it_matters: The lock persists across restarts and works while the device is offline, and it protects data without requiring a full wipe, giving defenders a middle-ground response to lost or compromised endpoints. It is in preview, so organisations may want to evaluate it before relying on it in production.

events.title: Microsoft says Copilot costs less than rivals in a study it funded and ran
events.summary: Microsoft funded and ran its own study concluding its Copilot AI assistant is cheaper than competing products, with the comparison covering usage charges as well as subscriptions. The result rests on chosen workloads and pricing assumptions, some of which are not published.
events.why_it_matters: For buyers of AI tools, the finding comes from an interested party and depends on selected workloads and pricing assumptions, including unpublished prices, so the cost comparison should be treated as vendor-sponsored rather than independent. It signals that per-usage charges, not just subscription fees, are becoming a factor in comparing assistant pricing.

events.why_it_matters: For buyers of AI video-analysis services, the record shows that listed prices alone may not reveal real costs, since included quantities are unspecified and Snowflake's table conflicts on the model version covered. Procurement teams comparing these two routes may need to confirm actual terms directly with vendors before committing.
